status: draft until committed with configs/experiments/S2_frozen.json before any s2_test episode; revised after the independent review (B1-B2, S1-S7, M1-M8) and after the calib spread pilot (S2-H3 pooled over three window-matched pairs)
authority: owner opened G-E08 and approved Reserve D ('Ja, beides', 2026-11-07) and asked to continue with E09-T02 ('Ja, weiter'); design by the agent; the batch budget needs a separate owner approval (configs/experiments/S2_approval.json)
question: When and why does VOI-driven re-observation lower a robot team's decision loss? Mechanism study in the simulator, not a new algorithm claim.

design.tuning: none: the configurations selected for X1/X2 (tuned at rate scale 1, cost ratio 4) are reused everywhere; the two new arms use repair's h5.0
design.replacement: an invalid scenario is replaced by the next unused entry of the same family behind the first b and takes the replaced building's slot; logged (amendment 01 O2, amendment 03 A1)

interventions.rate_scale: both passage rates times s in world and nominal model; pi = 1/3 fixed; s = 0 is the static cell
interventions.cost_ratio: false-open cost c on the policy level AND in the evaluation: it moves the decision threshold c/(c+1) of every arm, the VOI scoring of the repair arms and the loss scale together. It is a joint threshold-and-stakes manipulation, not a pure threshold change.

mechanism.window: after certainty a model-matched belief says 'open' for at most W = (1/k) ln((1-pi)/(theta-pi)); W = 47.6, 23.8, 11.9, 5.9 s at s = .25, .5, 1, 2 (c = 4) and 92.4, 46.2, 23.1, 11.6 s at c = 2
mechanism.derivation: a re-observation can change a later decision only while its information keeps the belief on the far side of the threshold, i.e. within about W after the reading. The fraction of requests a revisit can still affect grows with W relative to the travel and request times (5 s per robot), so the value of re-observation relative to frontier exploration should fall as W shrinks. As s -> 0 the window is unbounded but nothing changes, and re-observation only averages sensor noise; the gain need not be largest at s = 0 (an inverse U in s is possible and is not evidence against the account).
mechanism.limits: the VOI horizon of repair (5 s) is shorter than every W, so the window binds on the evaluation side, not inside the policy's scoring. H2 is predicted by most belief-ageing accounts and does not single out W; H3 is the discriminating test.

estimands.unit: building; per building and condition the mean over replicates; families 50/50
estimands.gain: per condition: 1 - M(L_arm) / M(L_reference), M the family-weighted mean of building means; a set of conditions is summarised by the unweighted mean of its per-condition gains (each condition counts equally, regardless of its loss level)
estimands.S2-H1: mean gain of repair_observe against no_comm over the 8 dynamic conditions (s > 0); the static conditions (s = 0) are reported separately and descriptively
estimands.S2-H2: mean gain of repair_observe against no_comm over both cost ratios at s = 0.25 minus the same at s = 2
estimands.S2-H3: window-matched contrast: mean over the three pairs with nearly equal window W but different cost ratio, gain of repair_observe against no_comm at (s=0.5, c=2; W 46.2 s) minus (s=0.25, c=4; 47.6 s), (s=1, c=2; 23.1 s) minus (s=0.5, c=4; 23.8 s), (s=2, c=2; 11.6 s) minus (s=1, c=4; 11.9 s); the window account predicts no difference although threshold and stakes differ
descriptive: per condition: mean loss, coverage (closed, final) and bytes of every arm; gains of repair, repair_observe, repair_send and age_revisit against no_comm, and of the repair arms against dynamics_ids (95 % intervals, unadjusted, not decisive)
Spearman rank correlation of the 8 dynamic per-condition gains (repair_observe vs no_comm) with W
counted decisions of the repair arms: observe_decisions and explore_decisions count decision steps (one trip spans several), send_frames counts evidence frames; the anchors have no counts
replication check: s = 1, c = 4 against the X1/X2 cell dyn-ind-direct for repair, no_comm, age_revisit and dynamics_ids
no additive attribution of repair's gain to observe and send without a model (E09-T02)
estimands.reading: repair_observe vs no_comm is VOI-driven revisiting plus frontier fallback against pure frontier, net of the exploration cost of revisits; age_revisit is the untargeted-revisit anchor

decision.family_wise: Bonferroni over S2-H1 to S2-H3: two-sided percentile intervals at 1 - 0.05/3 (0.8333 % and 99.1667 %); p-values are not used
decision.S2-H1 and S2-H2: supported if low > 0; against if high < 0.03 (no effect of interest); otherwise inconclusive
decision.S2-H3: consistent with the window account if the interval lies within [-0.03, 0.03]; against it if the interval excludes 0; otherwise inconclusive
decision.zero_reference: if the reference mean is 0 in the data or in any bootstrap draw for a quantity, its gain is undefined, the absolute difference is reported and the hypothesis is inconclusive

sample_size.rule: b = 100 (all fresh buildings). The MDE at 80 % power, MDE = (2.394 + 0.842) * sd / sqrt(b), comes from the calib spread pilot and is recorded here and in the approval. A large MDE is reported, never fixed by topping up.
sample_size.pilot: runs/s2_pilot_calib_v1 (docs/results/s2_pilot_calib_v1): 20 calib buildings, 1 replicate, 1 200 episodes, all ok; per-building contrasts with per-building ratio gains
sample_size.note: with 2 replicates the building-level sd shrinks by at most a factor sqrt(2); the one-replicate values are conservative. The pilot used calib buildings only; pooling S2-H3 over the three pre-specified window-matched pairs was decided from its spread, before any s2_test episode.

inference.bootstrap: paired cluster bootstrap over buildings, stratified by family, 10 000 draws, seed 20261107
inference.failure_rules: as preregistration v1 and amendment 01 (default 'closed' from the failure tick; killed episodes get coverage 0 by amendment 03 A2)
inference.stop: a budget stop evaluates the largest even prefix of slots complete for every arm and condition; below b_minimum the batch is inconclusive and is never topped up
inference.analysis: tools/analyze_s2.py, frozen by hash in configs/experiments/S2_frozen.json together with the whole source tree and tools/s2_batch.py, runs exactly once on the finished batch

reproduction: earlier analyses (X1/X2, X3) refuse to run at later commits because the source tree changed; they are reproduced at their own commits (966d2dc, 09d8ccc)
